summary: Separate boards license general contractors, residential builders, electricians, plumbers, HVAC contractors and electronic-security providers. Ordinary electrical permits and inspections are administered by city or county building departments.

electricalPermits.notes: Local requirements vary; Hoover's official electrical-permit page confirms local issuance and inspections. State-facility construction oversight is separate.

agencies.name: Alabama Licensing Board for General Contractors
agencies.notes: Commercial/general contractor licensing; residential homebuilding has a separate board. The roster provides a CSV download. Licensing exemptions changed October 1, 2026; consult the linked board notice.

agencies.name: Alabama Home Builders Licensure Board
agencies.notes: Residential building/remodeling and residential roofing licensing. Public verification is a board-hosted entry page to its vendor search.

agencies.name: Alabama Board of Electrical Contractors
agencies.notes: Licenses electrical contractors and journeymen.

agencies.name: Alabama Plumbers and Gas Fitters Examining Board
agencies.notes: Business verification; linked system also offers Individual Lookup for master/journeyman/apprentice credentials.

agencies.name: Alabama Board of Heating, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Contractors
agencies.notes: HVAC and commercial refrigeration contractor licensing.

agencies.name: Alabama Electronic Security Board of Licensure
agencies.notes: Security alarm, CCTV/access-control and locksmith regulation, subject to statutory exemptions; not a blanket license for all communications wiring. Current page publishes company and individual annual lists.

agencies.name: Alabama Department of Insurance — State Fire Marshal
agencies.notes: Fire alarm contractors require a separate Fire Marshal permit. The searchable approved-permit list verifies contractor credentials, not electrical construction project permits.

summary: Commerce registers construction contractors and licenses electrical and mechanical administrators; Labor issues electrician and plumber certificates of fitness. Labor conducts electrical inspections within its statutory scope, with Anchorage and Fairbanks exercising delegated local authority.

electricalPermits.program: Department of Labor and Workforce Development, Labor Standards and Safety, Mechanical Inspection
electricalPermits.notes: State electrical inspection covers commercial structures and dwellings of three units or more, with local inspection authority in Anchorage and Fairbanks under agreements. This is not universal state residential permitting.

agencies.name: Alaska Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development — Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing
agencies.notes: Registers construction contractors and licenses electrical and mechanical administrators; mechanical categories cover plumbing/HVAC and electrical categories govern applicable limited-energy work. Worker certificates of fitness are separate. Database download page offers professional-license CSV.

agencies.name: Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development — Mechanical Inspection
agencies.notes: Issues electrical and plumbing certificates of fitness and performs code inspections; also enforces contractor/administrator licensing for Commerce.

agencies.name: Alaska Department of Public Safety — Division of Fire and Life Safety, State Fire Marshal
agencies.notes: Fire-system technician permits cover applicable alarm-system installation, testing and maintenance. The official SmartGov portal provides credential reports and plan-review services; account-linked searches are not an unrestricted statewide electrical-permit database.

summary: The Registrar of Contractors licenses general and specialty construction businesses; the Board of Technical Registration separately regulates alarm businesses and agents. City and county building departments issue ordinary electrical permits and inspect the work.

electricalPermits.notes: Municipalities regulate work inside their boundaries; counties handle their unincorporated jurisdictions. Phoenix's current residential-permit page confirms electrical permitting.

agencies.name: Arizona Registrar of Contractors
agencies.notes: General, residential, commercial and specialty contractor licensing includes electrical, plumbing, HVAC/refrigeration and low-voltage work. Arizona does not issue a general statewide journeyman electrician or plumber license.

agencies.name: Arizona State Board of Technical Registration
agencies.notes: Registers alarm businesses and certifies applicable controlling persons and alarm agents; ROC construction licensing can also apply. The board advertises a new e-licensing portal in 2026.

summary: Labor and Licensing administers contractor, electrician and HVAC/R programs, while Health regulates plumbing and State Police regulates alarm companies. Electrical oversight is split between state inspectors and local permitting and inspection authorities.

electricalPermits.notes: Arkansas has no statewide electrical permit program. The Board of Electrical Examiners/ADLL administers electrician licensing and work standards only electrical permits and inspections are issued by local city/county building officials.

agencies.name: Arkansas Department of Labor and Licensing — Contractors Licensing Board and Residential Contractors Committee
agencies.notes: Commercial contractor licensing, residential builder/remodeler licensing, and applicable specialty/home-improvement registrations.

agencies.name: Arkansas Department of Labor and Licensing — Board of Electrical Examiners and Electrical Inspection and Licensing
agencies.notes: Licenses master/journeyman and applicable specialist electricians and electrical contractors; statewide inspection authority coexists with local inspection. April 2024 rules were accessible. Roster gateway was blocked and the historical official search presented user validation, so no working license lookup is claimed.

agencies.name: Arkansas Department of Labor and Licensing — HVAC/R Licensing Board
agencies.notes: Current program is at Labor and Licensing, not the older Department of Health location. Licenses HVAC/R contractors, registers technicians and supervises mechanical/fuel-gas inspections.

agencies.name: Arkansas Department of Health — Plumbing and Natural Gas, State Committee of Plumbing Examiners
agencies.notes: Regulates master/journeyman plumbers and apprentices and plumbing inspection.Main program homepage was blocked.

agencies.name: Arkansas Department of Public Safety — Arkansas State Police, Regulatory Services
agencies.notes: Licenses alarm installation/monitoring companies and applicable employees under private-security/alarm regulation. This is not a blanket license for all low-voltage communications wiring; electrical and contractor requirements may also apply.

agencies.name: Arkansas HVACR Licensing Board
agencies.notes: Full name: Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Licensing Board, within ADLL; the department provides HVACR contractor testing and license issuance (ADLL Code Enforcement HVAC-R page lists 501-682-9201 and 501-682-4553). The HVAC Roster page (recorded above) has a working searchable roster with CSV export.

summary: CSLB licenses general and specialty contractors, DIR certifies covered electrician employees, and BSIS regulates burglar-alarm businesses. Cities/counties handle ordinary electrical permits; HCAI administers permits for healthcare construction in its jurisdiction.

electricalPermits.notes: California has no statewide electrical permit or inspection program. Electrical permits are issued by city/county building departments (local AHJs); CSLB's official guidance confirms city and county permit issuance (Labor Code 3800, B&P 7031.5 require local permit offices to verify contractor licensure). No statewide permit search exists; permit lookup is per-jurisdiction. CSLB licenses the C-10 electrical contractor and DIR certifies the individual electricians, but neither issues permits.

agencies.name: California Department of Consumer Affairs — Contractors State License Board
agencies.notes: General A/B/B-2 and specialty licenses include C-10 electrical, C-36 plumbing, C-20 HVAC and C-7 low voltage. Fire-alarm installation falls under C-10; burglar alarms have separate BSIS regulation. Download page offers master contractor, personnel and workers-compensation files; exclusions include revoked, cancelled and nonrenewable expired licenses.

agencies.name: California Department of Industrial Relations — Division of Labor Standards Enforcement, Electrician Certification Unit
agencies.notes: Certifies covered electricians employed by C-10 contractors; categories include general, residential, fire/life safety, voice/data/video and nonresidential lighting. This is separate from CSLB business licensing. No equivalent statewide ordinary plumber or HVAC journeyman license was identified. Open-data catalog contains electrician-certification records.

agencies.name: California Department of Consumer Affairs — Bureau of Security and Investigative Services
agencies.notes: Regulates alarm company operators, qualified managers and alarm agents. Official verification gateway links to DCA search.

agencies.name: California Department of Health Care Access and Information — Office of Statewide Hospital Planning and Development
agencies.notes: Specialized healthcare-facility building permits and construction oversight include electrical work within HCAI jurisdiction. OSHPD remains the building-safety office name within HCAI.

summary: DORA regulates electrical and plumbing contractors and workers, and issues permits where a qualifying local authority does not. There is no statewide general-building or HVAC contractor license; cities and counties impose their own requirements.

electricalPermits.program: Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies — Division of Professions and Occupations, Electrical and Plumbing Inspections
electricalPermits.notes: The state permit search explicitly excludes cities/counties using their own inspection programs. Qualified state higher-education institutions may also administer their own program. Search by permit number or street address and city.

agencies.name: Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies — State Electrical Board
agencies.notes: Registers electrical contractors and licenses master, journeyman and residential wireman electricians; apprentices register.Dataset is a published extract, not a replacement for live license verification.

agencies.name: Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies — State Plumbing Board
agencies.notes: Registers plumbing contractors and licenses master, journeyman and residential plumbers; apprentices register. State plumbing permits share the electrical permit search.

agencies.name: City of Boulder — Planning and Development Services; Fire-Rescue contractor licensing
agencies.notes: Local example only, not a statewide regulator. Building, mechanical and fire-system contractor licensing is municipal; this page includes Find a Licensed Contractor. Low-voltage/alarm requirements depend on system and locality. No separate statewide comprehensive low-voltage/alarm-business credential was verified; do not infer that all such wiring is exempt from electrical licensing.

agencies.name: Colorado State Electrical Board (DORA Division of Professions and Occupations)
agencies.notes: Licenses residential wiremen, journeyman electricians, and master electricians; registers electrical contractor businesses (a registered contractor must employ a licensed master electrician as responsible individual). SB 25-165 adds a Photovoltaic Installer registration due Dec 31, 2026. State electrical permits are issued through DPO's Electrical & Plumbing Permits program (see separate entry).

summary: Consumer Protection registers home-improvement, new-home and major contractors and licenses the construction trades, including limited electrical/alarm work. Municipal building officials handle ordinary electrical permits; DAS handles covered state construction.

electricalPermits.notes: No state electrical permit program exists. Electrical permits are issued by city/town building departments (verified example: City of Bridgeport Building Department electrical permit page, which requires a CT electrical license e.g. E-1). Statewide trade licensing is separate and handled by DCP. There is no state permit search portal because permits are local.

agencies.name: Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection — Occupational and Professional Licensing and trade examining boards
agencies.notes: Administers home-improvement and new-home contractor registrations plus major-contractor registration for threshold buildings; there is no single unrestricted general contractor license covering all work. Electrical, plumbing/pipefitting, heating/cooling and related boards license contractors and workers. E-1/E-2 general electrical and C/L limited classifications govern applicable low-voltage and alarm work. eLicense also offers downloadable rosters; Socrata contains state licenses/credentials.

agencies.name: Connecticut Department of Administrative Services — Office of the State Building Inspector
agencies.notes: State construction permit/inspection authority, not trade licensing.

summary: Labor registers construction contractors, Revenue licenses businesses, and Professional Regulation licenses electrical, plumbing and HVAC trades. Electrical compliance combines licensed private inspection agencies, local construction approvals and state homeowner electrical permits.

electricalPermits.program: Delaware Division of Professional Regulation — Board of Electrical Examiners; licensed electrical inspection agencies
electricalPermits.notes: The Board issues homeowner electrical permits and licenses inspection agencies; electrical work is inspected by licensed inspection agencies rather than a Washington-style statewide government field force. Local building permits may also apply.

agencies.name: Delaware Department of Labor — Division of Industrial Affairs, Office of Construction Enforcement / Contractor Registration
agencies.notes: Construction-services contractors must register before public or private work begins. Current program page places contractor registration within the Office of Construction Enforcement; One Stop retains Office of Contractor Registration terminology. Registration is separate from trade competency and Revenue business licenses.

agencies.name: Delaware Department of Finance — Division of Revenue
agencies.notes: Issues contractor business licenses for tax/business purposes, not a general-building competency license.

agencies.name: Delaware Division of Professional Regulation — Board of Electrical Examiners
agencies.notes: Licenses electricians and electrical inspection agencies; master/specialty credentials govern contracting and applicable low-voltage work. Issues homeowner electrical permits. Website is the board's official homeowner-permit program page. Open licensing dataset includes multiple credential types; not a complete project-permit database.

agencies.name: Delaware Division of Professional Regulation — Board of Plumbing, Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Examiners
agencies.notes: Master plumber and HVACR/master restricted HVACR credentials authorize the relevant trade work. Apprenticeship and contractor business registration are distinct. Dataset is shared across DPR professions.

agencies.name: Delaware State Police — Professional Licensing Section
agencies.notes: Licenses security-system/protective-service alarm businesses and applicable employees.Alarm-user registrations are not installer credentials.

agencies.name: Delaware Office of the State Fire Marshal
agencies.notes: Separately licenses fire-alarm/fire-protection companies and certificate holders, including applicable monitoring work.

summary: DLCP handles business and occupational construction licensing; DOB handles District-wide electrical permits and inspections. The former DCRA's licensing and building functions are now split between these departments.

electricalPermits.program: District of Columbia Department of Buildings — Permits and Construction
electricalPermits.notes: The District is a single jurisdiction, so state denotes District-wide issuance rather than a state/local fallback arrangement. DOB issues electrical systems-installation trade permits and administers inspections, including authorized third-party inspection arrangements. eRecords is the official public records gateway; individual searches were not executed.

agencies.name: District of Columbia Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection — Business Licensing and Board of Industrial Trades
agencies.notes: Business licenses cover construction businesses; Industrial Trades regulates electrical, plumbing/gas and refrigeration/air-conditioning trades, including applicable low-voltage electrical classes. Alarm installation requires applicable trade authorization; security-guard credentials are separate.DCRA split occurred in 2022. DLCP advertises BEST Act licensing changes and the BOSS portal launch in August 2026, so historical business-category labels should not be assumed current.

agencies.name: District of Columbia Department of Buildings
agencies.notes: Issues building and electrical/plumbing/mechanical trade permits.eRecords provides public records access. Open Data DC's 2025 building-permit layer is an annual permit dataset, not a verified complete all-years electrical-only extract.

summary: DBPR's construction and electrical boards license general and trade contractors, including alarm contractors. Cities and counties issue ordinary electrical permits and inspect the work; Florida does not issue a general statewide journeyman-electrician license.

electricalPermits.notes: Local building departments administer ordinary electrical permits under the Florida Building Code; specialized state facilities have separate oversight. No statewide ordinary electrical-permit search. Miami-Dade's official page documents local electrical permitting and inspections.

agencies.name: Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation — Construction Industry Licensing Board
agencies.notes: Licenses general/building/residential and specialty construction contractors, including plumbing, air conditioning and mechanical. Certified licenses authorize statewide practice; registered licenses depend on local competency/jurisdiction. Local journeyman requirements are separate. Public-records page offers downloadable licensee files and explains status exclusions; no state construction permit database here.

agencies.name: Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation — Electrical Contractors' Licensing Board
agencies.notes: Electrical and applicable specialty/limited-energy contractors; alarm system contractor I includes fire alarms and II excludes fire alarms. Contractor credentials and qualified businesses are distinct from local journeyman licensing and employee alarm-agent training requirements.

agencies.name: Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services - Division of Licensing
agencies.notes: Licenses and regulates the private security industry under Ch. 493 FS: security agencies (Class B), security officers (Class D), managers (Class M/MB), firearms (Class G), plus private investigators and recovery agents. Alarm system (burglar/fire alarm) contracting itself is licensed by DBPR/ECLB, not FDACS. The license lookup pages (Verify-a-License and /Business-Services/Check-A-License) returned HTTP 200 from the official site but are JavaScript-rendered, so only the site frame could be captured - flagged per reporting rules. Main phone could not be captured from fetched pages (only the Custodian of Records line (850) 245-1000 appeared on the Contact Us page).

agencies.name: Florida Department of Financial Services - Division of State Fire Marshal, Bureau of Fire Prevention, Regulatory Licensing Section
agencies.notes: Licenses Fire Protection System Contractors I-V, Water-Based Fire Protection System Inspector permits, fire equipment dealers/service technicians, explosives and sparklers (Ch.This is fire sprinkler/special-hazard contracting, distinct from burglar-alarm contractors (DBPR/ECLB) and private security (FDACS).Address: 200 E. Gaines Street, Tallahassee, FL 32399-0342.

summary: Secretary of State licensing boards regulate residential/general contractors and the electrical, plumbing, conditioned-air and low-voltage trades. City and county building departments issue ordinary electrical permits and perform inspections.

electricalPermits.notes: State contractor licensing does not make the state the ordinary electrical-permit issuer.

agencies.name: Georgia Secretary of State — State Licensing Board for Residential and General Contractors
agencies.notes: Residential Basic, Residential-Light Commercial and General Contractor licensure; qualifying-agent/business relationships matter.

agencies.name: Georgia Secretary of State — State Construction Industry Licensing Board, Division of Electrical Contractors
agencies.notes: Class I restricted and Class II unrestricted electrical contractor licenses. No separate general statewide journeyman-electrician license.

agencies.name: Georgia Secretary of State — State Construction Industry Licensing Board, Division of Master and Journeyman Plumbers
agencies.notes: Licenses journeyman and master plumbers; master license classifications govern contracting scope.

agencies.name: Georgia Secretary of State — State Construction Industry Licensing Board, Division of Conditioned Air Contractors
agencies.notes: Conditioned-air contractor Class I restricted/Class II unrestricted credentials cover applicable heating and air-conditioning work.

agencies.name: Georgia Secretary of State — State Construction Industry Licensing Board, Division of Low Voltage Contractors
agencies.notes: Low-voltage licenses include alarm, general, telecommunications and unrestricted categories. Alarm installation belongs here rather than the private-security-guard licensing board.

agencies.name: Georgia Department of Community Affairs - Office of Construction Codes and Industrialized Buildings
agencies.notes: Not a licensing agency. The Board of Community Affairs adopts Georgia's mandatory state minimum standard codes under O.C.G.A. 8-2-23 (current: 2024 IBC/IRC/IMC/IPC/IFGC, 2023 NEC with 2026 Georgia amendments, per fetched DCA pages; new 2026 NEC amendments adopted for Jan 1, 2027). Code enforcement and all construction/electrical permits and inspections are performed by local city/county building departments. DCA also administers the industrialized (modular) buildings approval program. Phone (404) 679-3118 from fetched DCA announcement and Lee County, GA notice.

summary: DCCA's Contractors License Board licenses general and specialty businesses, while its electricians/plumbers board licenses those individual tradespeople. County building departments issue electrical permits and inspect construction.

electricalPermits.notes: County building departments in Honolulu, Hawaii, Maui and Kauai administer ordinary construction permitting and electrical inspections.

agencies.name: Hawaii Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs — Professional and Vocational Licensing, Contractors License Board
agencies.notes: General engineering/building and specialty businesses/qualifying responsible managing employees. Classes include C-13 electrical, C-37 plumbing, C-52 ventilation/air conditioning, C-40 refrigeration, C-15 electronic systems, C-15a fire/burglar alarms and C-15b telecommunications.

agencies.name: Hawaii Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs — Professional and Vocational Licensing, Board of Electricians and Plumbers
agencies.notes: Licenses individual journey-worker/supervising electricians and journey-worker/master plumbers, separately from contractor-business licensing.

agencies.name: Hawaii Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs, Professional and Vocational Licensing Division - Board of Private Detective and Guards
agencies.notes: Hawaii's only security-industry board; it licenses private detectives, guards, guard employees, and detective/guard agencies. It does NOT license alarm installers — burglar/fire alarm installation is regulated through the Contractors License Board's C-15a (fire and burglar alarm) and C-15 (electronic systems) classifications. Listed because it is the closest state analog to a private security board.

summary: DOPL registers general contractors and administers electrical, plumbing, HVAC and public-works contractor boards. Its electrical program issues permits and inspects where an authorized local program does not.

electricalPermits.program: Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses — Electrical Program

agencies.name: Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses — Contractors Board
agencies.notes: General construction contractor registration is not an examination-based general contractor license. Specialized state trade licenses and public-works licenses are separate.

agencies.name: Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses — Public Works Contractors License Board
agencies.notes: Licenses contractors for covered public-works projects by type/class; distinct from ordinary contractor registration.

agencies.name: Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses — Idaho Electrical Board
agencies.notes: Electrical contractors and applicable master/journeyman/specialty workers are licensed; apprentices register. Limited-energy classifications cover applicable fire/security alarms and other systems, with statutory/rule exemptions.DOPL is the current authority; older Division of Building Safety branding remains on some portals.

agencies.name: Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses — State Plumbing Board
agencies.notes: Licenses plumbing contractors and workers and administers state plumbing permits/inspections within its jurisdiction.

agencies.name: Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses — Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning Board
agencies.notes: Licenses HVAC contractors, journeymen and applicable specialties, registers apprentices, and administers state HVAC permits/inspections within its jurisdiction.

summary: There is no statewide general-contractor, electrician or ordinary HVAC contractor license; cities and counties set local requirements and handle electrical permits. IDPH regulates plumbing, while IDFPR regulates roofing and private-alarm contractors.

electricalPermits.notes: Ordinary electrical permits and inspections are municipal/county responsibilities, with requirements varying by jurisdiction.

agencies.name: Illinois Department of Public Health — Plumbing Program
agencies.notes: Licenses plumbers/apprentices and registers plumbing contractors, with Chicago licensing/reciprocity provisions.

agencies.name: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation — Division of Professional Regulation
agencies.notes: State construction specialty includes roofing, not general contractors. Private alarm contractor, agency and applicable employee credentials cover security/fire-alarm services; this is not blanket licensing of all low-voltage wiring. CORE licensing transition began in 2024.

agencies.name: City of Chicago — Department of Buildings
agencies.notes: Local example only.Chicago licenses electrical contractors locally and has separate plumber licensing recognized in IDPH reciprocity provisions; a Chicago credential is not a statewide electrician license.

agencies.name: Office of the Illinois State Fire Marshal
agencies.notes: Licenses fire sprinkler contractors and fire sprinkler inspectors statewide (Fire Sprinkler Contractor Licensing Act, 225 ILCS 317; 41 Ill. Adm. Code 109) and fire equipment distributors/employees who service extinguishers and fixed suppression systems (Fire Equipment Distributor and Employee Regulation Act, 41 Ill. Adm. Code 251); also licenses underground storage tank (UST) contractors. Per its own FAQ, OSFM does NOT license fire alarm contractors - that is IDFPR's role. Toll-free line also shown on site: (866) 324-3841. No public license lookup page found on the OSFM site.

summary: Indiana licenses plumbers through the Professional Licensing Agency, but general, electrical and HVAC contractor requirements are local. Local departments issue electrical permits; Homeland Security separately reviews covered Class 1 construction plans.

electricalPermits.notes: State Class 1 construction design release is separate from an ordinary electrical trade permit.

agencies.name: Indiana Professional Licensing Agency — Indiana Plumbing Commission
agencies.notes: Licenses plumbing contractors/journeyman plumbers and registers apprentices. State business guide identifies plumbing as the statewide construction trade licensing exception; general, electrical and HVAC requirements are local.Downloadable license files are sold, so they are not listed as free open data.

agencies.name: Indiana Department of Homeland Security — Building Plan Review
agencies.notes: Reviews covered Class 1 construction and issues construction design releases, including relevant electrical/mechanical systems.

agencies.name: City of Logansport — Building Commissioner
agencies.notes: Local example only: contractor registration, electrical licenses and building permits are administered through the city's linked OpenGov service.

summary: DIAL registers construction contractors and administers the electrical, plumbing/mechanical and alarm licensing programs. The state electrical program issues permits and inspects outside approved local inspection jurisdictions.

electricalPermits.program: Iowa Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing — Electrical Examining Board and Electrical Inspection Program
electricalPermits.notes: DIAL's electrical portal provides separate public license and permit searches. Local approved inspection programs retain their jurisdiction. Legacy DPS and IDPH hostnames remain in official links after the July 1, 2023 DIAL reorganization.

agencies.name: Iowa Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing — Contractor Registration
agencies.notes: Construction businesses earning at least $2,000 annually generally register; this is not a general-building competency license. Official program page is a verification gateway; direct legacy contractor search was inaccessible. Iowa Data Hub offers a downloadable active contractor-registration dataset, distinct from electrical/plumbing license records.

agencies.name: Iowa Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing — Electrical Examining Board and Electrical Inspection Program
agencies.notes: Licenses electrical contractors and applicable master/journeyman/residential/special electrical workers; apprentice registrations are separate.Low-voltage exemptions and alarm licensing must be evaluated separately.

agencies.name: Iowa Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing — Plumbing and Mechanical Systems Board
agencies.notes: Licenses plumbing, HVAC/refrigeration, hydronic and related mechanical contractors and individual master/journey/apprentice/specialty credentials. Contractors also need DIAL registration. Official public-search link redirects to this JavaScript portal; search execution was not tested.

agencies.name: Iowa Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing — Alarm Systems Licensing
agencies.notes: Licenses applicable alarm companies and individual installers for fire, security and other regulated alarm systems. Electrical-license exemptions are limited and do not automatically authorize every alarm installation task.

summary: Kansas has no statewide general-contractor, electrician, plumbing or HVAC license; municipalities and counties administer local licensing and electrical permits. The Attorney General registers roofers, and the State Fire Marshal requires registration of fire-alarm/sprinkler companies.

electricalPermits.notes: Local building departments issue electrical permits and perform inspections. The 2026 HB 2588 proposal for statewide electrician licensing is marked Died on the Legislature's current bill page; it is not an operating state licensing/permit program.

agencies.name: Kansas Attorney General — Roofing Registration Unit
agencies.notes: Registers commercial/residential roofing contractors, not general contractors. Current statute confirms this authority.

agencies.name: Kansas Office of the State Fire Marshal
agencies.notes: Official page explicitly distinguishes registration from licensing: fire-alarm and sprinkler companies must register, but OSFM does not issue those company licenses. The role label represents this registration duty.

agencies.name: Wichita–Sedgwick County Metropolitan Area Building and Construction Department
agencies.notes: Local example only: licensing and permits apply within MABCD's participating city/county jurisdictions, not all Kansas. The official portal provides public search access. Low-voltage/fire-alarm work must be checked against local trade rules and the separate OSFM registration requirement.

agencies.name: Kansas Attorney General's Office
agencies.notes: Under the Kansas Roofing Registration Act (K.S.A. 50-6,122, effective July 1, 2013), every roofing contractor must obtain a registration certificate from the Attorney General before providing commercial or residential roofing services for a fee in Kansas; it is a registration, not a competency license.No state agency licenses general contractors, electricians, plumbers, HVAC, or alarm/low-voltage contractors in Kansas - those are handled (where at all) by home-rule cities and counties; no official state open-data dataset of local licenses was found.

summary: Kentucky has no statewide general contractor license; city/county requirements apply. DHBC licenses electrical, plumbing and HVAC trades, with electrical permitting divided between local authorities and the state.

electricalPermits.program: Department of Housing, Buildings and Construction — Electrical Division
electricalPermits.notes: Local governments ordinarily arrange electrical permits and certified inspections. Under 815 KAR 35:020, DHBC inspects when a local certified inspector is unavailable, on state-owned property, and in certain additional state-review cases. SmartGov is an application portal; its notice directs private-property applicants to their local authority.

agencies.name: Kentucky Department of Housing, Buildings and Construction
agencies.notes: Electrical Division licenses electrical contractors, master electricians and electricians; plumbing and HVAC divisions license their respective master/journeyman trades. KRS 227A.150 authorizes a low-voltage installer certificate for qualifying Class 2/3 power-limited work; the statute alone does not verify current issuance procedures. General contractors are regulated locally, not licensed by DHBC. No official bulk license/permit dataset was verified.

agencies.name: Kentucky Department of Housing, Buildings and Construction — State Fire Marshal
agencies.notes: DHBC identifies fire-alarm and sprinkler contractor licensing among its functions. This is fire-protection licensing, not proof of a general burglar-alarm/security business license.No official bulk license/permit dataset was verified.

summary: LSLBC licenses construction and specialty contracting businesses; the plumbing board licenses plumbers and the State Fire Marshal licenses alarm/security firms and personnel. Electrical permits and inspections are administered by parish or municipal authorities.

electricalPermits.notes: No general state-issued electrical permit/inspection program was verified. Local parish/city building departments are the electrical permitting authorities; state fire/life-safety plan review is a separate function.

agencies.name: Louisiana State Licensing Board for Contractors
agencies.notes: Commercial/residential contracting and home-improvement registration are scope/value dependent. Electrical, mechanical and plumbing classifications cover contracting businesses, not a statewide journeyman electrician credential; individual electrical qualifications may be local. Telecommunications/low-voltage is a specialty classification.No official bulk license/permit dataset was verified.

agencies.name: State Plumbing Board of Louisiana
agencies.notes: Licenses master/journeyman/residential plumbers and natural-gas fitters; registers apprentices. HVAC role here is limited to regulated gas-fitting work. Its site announces a transition to LSLBC under Act 908 of 2026; retain this separately verified roster while the transition is in progress. No official bulk license/permit dataset was verified.

agencies.name: Louisiana Office of State Fire Marshal — Life Safety and Property Protection
agencies.notes: Licenses fire-alarm and security-system firms and personnel, including relevant CCTV/access-control activities.Website is the official program page, not a commercial directory. No official bulk license/permit dataset was verified.

agencies.name: City of New Orleans — Department of Safety & Permits (local example)
agencies.notes: Local example of where Louisiana's trade licensing/permits actually happen for individuals: NOLA licenses electrical contractors (Class 'A' required to pull electrical permits; Electrical & Mechanical Contractors License line (504) 658-7107) and issues electrical permits/inspections (Permit Intake (504) 658-7299). New Orleans publishes a 'Permits - BLDS' open dataset on data.nola.gov (Socrata dataset id 72f9-bi28, includes contractor license fields; verified via Socrata catalog API). Other cities/parishes (Baton Rouge, Shreveport, Jefferson Parish, etc.) run their own programs.

summary: Maine does not license general home-construction contractors statewide. OPOR's electricians, plumbers and fuel boards regulate trades; the Electricians' Examining Board issues electrical permits where there is no local electrical inspection program.

electricalPermits.program: Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation — Electricians' Examining Board
electricalPermits.notes: Municipalities with their own electrical inspection programs issue local permits. State permit requirements have exceptions, including qualifying single-family dwelling certification by a master electrician; do not treat every job outside a municipal program as requiring a state permit.

agencies.name: Maine Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation — Electricians' Examining Board
agencies.notes: Licenses master, journeyman, limited, helper and apprentice electricians. Contracting authority is tied to the appropriate master/limited license rather than a general construction company license.Low-voltage work has scope-dependent exemptions; no separate general alarm/security installer board was verified.

agencies.name: Maine Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation — Plumbers' Examining Board
agencies.notes: Licenses master and journeyman plumbers and trainees.

agencies.name: Maine Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation — Maine Fuel Board
agencies.notes: Regulates oil/solid-fuel technicians and propane/natural-gas technicians. Maine has no single all-purpose HVAC contractor credential: fuel, plumbing and electrical licenses apply by scope, with municipal mechanical permitting.

agencies.name: Maine Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Program

agencies.name: New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
agencies.notes: Licenses Home Improvement Contractor businesses (work on residential property over $200; NYC Admin Code §20-386, exam + $20k bond or Trust Fund). Lookup links to a 'Search Business' web app (no login needed). Renamed from Department of Consumer Affairs (DCA) in 2019 (Local Law 80 of 2020), so site URLs still use /site/dca/. Renewals line: (212) 487-4060.

agencies.name: Nassau County Department of Consumer Affairs (county-level example)
agencies.notes: Example of county-level licensing: licenses Home Improvement Contractors under Nassau County Administrative Code §21-11 (Licensing Division); the licensing page (nassaucountyny.Suffolk, Westchester, Rockland, Putnam and Orange counties run similar county HIC programs. Phone not shown on fetched pages (county site WAF intermittently rejects fetches).

summary: North Carolina has separate boards for general, electrical, plumbing/heating/fire-sprinkler and refrigeration contractors, plus a Security Systems Licensing Board. Local inspection departments issue ordinary electrical permits; OSFM has special state electrical inspection duties.

electricalPermits.notes: No state electrical permit or inspection program exists in NC. City/county inspections departments issue electrical permits and perform inspections under the NC Electrical Code (official example: Mecklenburg County Code Enforcement issues building, electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits for Charlotte and all of Mecklenburg County per NCGS 160D-1110; see State-level boards license the contractors but do not permit or inspect work.

agencies.name: North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors
agencies.notes: Licenses general contractors for projects within statutory scope, generally $40,000 or more. Residential/building classifications and license limitations matter. This board is separate from the trade boards. No official bulk license/permit dataset was verified.

agencies.name: North Carolina State Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors
agencies.notes: Licenses electrical contracting businesses through qualified individuals; there is no general statewide journeyman electrician license from this board. Special restricted fire-alarm/low-voltage classification covers its defined scope. Security-system work may also require the separate Security Systems Licensing Board credential. No official bulk license/permit dataset was verified.

agencies.name: North Carolina State Board of Examiners of Plumbing, Heating and Fire Sprinkler Contractors
agencies.notes: Licenses plumbing, heating and fire-sprinkler contracting and designated technician classes. General refrigeration contracting is separately regulated; do not substitute one board's search for the other. No official bulk license/permit dataset was verified.

agencies.name: North Carolina State Board of Refrigeration Contractors
agencies.notes: Separate refrigeration contractor licensing; scope/exemptions distinguish this board from heating/HVAC credentials. No official bulk license/permit dataset was verified.

agencies.name: North Carolina Department of Public Safety — Security Systems Licensing Board
agencies.notes: Current name is Security Systems Licensing Board, formerly Alarm Systems Licensing Board. Regulates covered security-system businesses and personnel.No official bulk license/permit dataset was verified.

agencies.name: North Carolina Office of State Fire Marshal — State Electrical Division
agencies.notes: Separate state code/inspection program, including designated transportation electrical inspections; local building departments remain the ordinary electrical permit issuers. No current public state permit lookup or downloadable permit dataset was verified.

agencies.name: NC State Board of Refrigeration Contractors
agencies.notes: Separate board that licenses refrigeration contractors (NCGS Ch. 87 Art. 5), distinct from heating/HVAC licenses issued by the Plumbing/Heating/Fire Sprinkler board. Lookup is a search-form web app; no open-data dataset found. Office: 1027 US 70 Hwy W, Suite 221, Garner, NC.

summary: The Secretary of State licenses construction contractors; separate electrical and plumbing boards license the trades. NDSEB administers wiring certificates and inspections, with municipal electrical programs also operating.

electricalPermits.program: North Dakota State Electrical Board (NDSEB) Electrical Wiring Certificate / E-Cert program
electricalPermits.notes: ND Admin Code 24.1-05-01-01 requires an electrical wiring certificate filed with the State Electrical Board for all electrical installations (including power-limited systems) valued at $500 or more; the supervising master, class B, or power-limited electrician files the certificate and the state collects the inspection fee. State electrical inspectors cover 14-15 assigned districts statewide, but the cities of Bismarck, Fargo, and Grand Forks operate their own city electrical inspection departments (listed on NDSEB's Inspection Districts page), so inspection is local there while certificates still go through the board (e.g., Minot's self-wire form notes fees are invoiced by NDSEB).Note: NDSEB is replacing its online licensing/permit system Jan 29 - Feb 3, 2027 (announced on its site).

agencies.name: North Dakota Secretary of State
agencies.notes: Construction contractor license required above $4,000, including general contractors and subcontractors. FirstStop is the official contractor search. HVAC firms may need this contractor license; separate mechanical licensing is municipal, such as Bismarck.Does not issue electrical permits.

agencies.name: North Dakota State Electrical Board
agencies.notes: Licenses contracting master electricians and individual electricians, including contracting/noncontracting power-limited electricians. Low-voltage and alarm wiring must be evaluated under power-limited electrical scope and exemptions; this is not a separate private-security agency license. Separate individual-electrician search is included in sources.

agencies.name: North Dakota State Plumbing Board
agencies.notes: Licenses master and journeyman plumbers and registers apprentices; contractor business licensing is additionally through SOS.

summary: There is no statewide general-contractor license; municipalities set local contractor and residential-trade requirements. OCILB licenses commercial electrical, plumbing, HVAC, refrigeration and hydronics contractors, while state or certified local building departments handle electrical approvals and inspections.

electricalPermits.program: Ohio Department of Commerce, Division of Industrial Compliance — Building Code Compliance
electricalPermits.notes: State building-code enforcement covers nonresidential construction where there is no certified local building department and specified state projects; this is not a statewide residential electrical-permit service.

agencies.name: Ohio Department of Commerce — Ohio Construction Industry Licensing Board
agencies.notes: State licenses are issued to qualifying individuals for commercial contracting and associated with contracting companies. Ohio has no universal statewide journeyman-electrician license; residential and individual-trade requirements may be local. Under ORC 4740.13(D), listed alarm/communications systems below 50 volts are outside OCILB electrical-contractor licensing, without removing separate fire-alarm certification requirements. Website is the official licensing portal homepage because informational Commerce pages failed to open.

agencies.name: Ohio Department of Commerce — Division of Industrial Compliance, Building Code Compliance
agencies.notes: Handles state-jurisdiction electrical plan approval and inspection.Website, public permit search and main phone remain unconfirmed. This unit does not issue the OCILB contractor credential.

agencies.name: Ohio Department of Commerce — Division of State Fire Marshal
agencies.notes: Fire-protection company and individual certifications include fire-alarm work; these do not establish a general statewide burglar-alarm installer license.

agencies.name: Ohio Homeland Security — Private Investigator Security Guard Services (Ohio Department of Public Safety)
agencies.notes: PISGS licenses and regulates private investigation and security-guard SERVICES COMPANIES (Class A/B/C licenses under ORC 4749) and registers their employees (~800 providers, ~24,000 registered employees) — this is the private-security side of 'alarm/security' licensing, not alarm-system installation. Reorganization note: the program moved from the Dept. of Commerce (Real Estate & Professional Licensing) to the Dept. of Public Safety in 2004 and now operates as a component of Ohio Homeland Security (whose site hosts it; www.pisgs.ohio.gov also resolves to the same content).

summary: Oklahoma has no statewide general-contractor license; cities and other local jurisdictions set local requirements. CIB licenses electrical, plumbing and mechanical trades, ODOL licenses alarm/security work, and electrical work permits are issued locally.

electricalPermits.notes: CIB expressly does not issue work permits. Local jurisdictions issue electrical permits and conduct local inspections; CIB investigates and can inspect outside local inspection programs, where notification of work may be required. State inspection authority should not be mistaken for a state electrical-permit program.

agencies.name: Oklahoma Construction Industries Board
agencies.notes: No statewide general-contractor license. contractor_license here denotes roofing-contractor registration, not general construction. Licenses electrical, plumbing and mechanical contractors and individual tradespeople.CIB does not issue electrical permits.

agencies.name: Oklahoma Department of Labor — Alarm, Locksmith and Fire Sprinkler Program
agencies.notes: Regulates alarm/security companies and individual personnel, including licensed alarm and electronic-security categories; ordinary low-voltage data cabling should not automatically be classified as alarm work.

summary: CCB licenses construction businesses, while the Building Codes Division licenses electricians, electrical contractors, plumbers and plumbing contractors. Local building departments issue most electrical permits; BCD serves areas without local programs.

electricalPermits.program: Oregon Department of Consumer and Business Services — Building Codes Division
electricalPermits.notes: BCD provides electrical permitting/inspection services in designated counties and administers statewide minor-label programs.

agencies.name: Oregon Construction Contractors Board
agencies.notes: Licenses residential/commercial general and specialty construction businesses. HVAC construction is covered by the appropriate CCB business endorsement, not a separate universal HVAC-technician license. Electrical and plumbing businesses also need applicable BCD credentials. Socrata dataset is CCB Active Licenses. CCB does not issue electrical permits.

agencies.name: Oregon Building Codes Division, Department of Consumer and Business Services
agencies.notes: Licenses individual electricians/plumbers and electrical/plumbing contractors, including limited-energy electrical categories. Class A limited-energy scope includes protective signaling such as fire/security alarms; limited licenses are scope-specific. HVAC electrical connections may require an applicable electrical credential.BCD Active Contractor/Individual Licenses is the official open dataset. Public ePermitting destination could not be verified by opening.

agencies.name: Oregon Department of Public Safety Standards and Training
agencies.notes: Administers the Private Security Program: certifies private security professionals (unarmed, armed, and alarm monitor categories) and licenses private security entities (security businesses) under ORS 181A.840-995; also licenses private investigators and polygraph examiners. The license lookup is DPSST's IRIS/SnapShot records system ('SMS Entity Search' for Private Security Entities); it is DPSST's official public records system but is hosted on bpl-orsnapshot.net rather than a.gov domain (linked from DPSST pages). Private Security program direct line: 503-378-8531. Individual professional certification lookup is via the IRIS 'Information Records Inquiry System' linked from the Private Security pages. Some counties/cities (e.g., Lincoln County) additionally require local alarm-installer licenses. No state open-data dataset found for DPSST licenses.

summary: Pennsylvania has no statewide general-contractor or general electrical, plumbing or HVAC trade license; local governments impose applicable licensing requirements. The Attorney General registers covered home-improvement contractors, while UCC electrical enforcement is divided among municipalities, certified third parties and state Labor & Industry.

electricalPermits.program: Pennsylvania Department of Labor & Industry — Uniform Construction Code
electricalPermits.notes: Opt-in municipalities enforce the UCC, directly or through certified third parties. In opt-out municipalities, DLI handles covered nonresidential construction and owners arrange certified third-party residential enforcement. DLI also handles state-owned building jurisdiction.

agencies.name: Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General — Home Improvement Contractor Registration
agencies.notes: HICPA registration is not a statewide construction competency license and does not cover all new-home or commercial construction. Electrical, plumbing and HVAC firms doing covered home improvements may need registration plus applicable local trade credentials.Electrical permits are not issued by OAG.

agencies.name: Pennsylvania Department of Labor & Industry — Bureau of Occupational and Industrial Safety
agencies.notes: UCC permitting and inspection responsibilities depend on municipal election and building type. No statewide electrician, plumbing, HVAC or general low-voltage/alarm-installer license was identified in the contractor-licensing guidance; municipal licensing and fire/building approvals remain relevant. Not a trade-license lookup agency.

summary: The Contractors' Registration and Licensing Board registers construction contractors, and DLT licenses electrical, plumbing, mechanical and alarm/telecommunications trades. Municipalities issue ordinary electrical permits; the state Building Code Commission handles projects within state-building jurisdiction.

electricalPermits.notes: No statewide electrical permit or state electrical inspection program exists in Rhode Island. Electrical permits are issued and inspected by each municipality's building official/inspections department (e.g., the Town of Coventry's Building Official page explicitly schedules building, electrical, mechanical and plumbing inspections locally). The RI State Building Code Commission (in DBR's State Building Office) adopts the codes but enforcement is local; DBR only permits certain state-regulated facilities. Accordingly there is no state permit lookup; towns use their own portals (Coventry uses coventryri.viewpointcloud.com).

agencies.name: Rhode Island Contractors' Registration and Licensing Board, Department of Business Regulation
agencies.notes: Registers residential/commercial contractors and licenses specified specialties, including commercial roofing. Separate DLT trade licensing remains necessary.CRLB does not issue electrical permits.

agencies.name: Rhode Island Department of Labor and Training — Professional Regulation
agencies.notes: Administers electrical contractor/master and journeyman licensing, plumbing, refrigeration/pipefitting and other mechanical trades, telecommunications, and burglar-alarm business/agent credentials. Website is the program homepage; the department root failed to open.No electrical-permit search administered by this licensing unit.

agencies.name: Rhode Island Building Code Commission — State Building Office, Department of Business Regulation
agencies.notes: State Building Office issues building and related electrical/mechanical/plumbing permits within its state-property jurisdiction.

summary: LLR's Contractor's Licensing Board licenses commercial general/mechanical contractors and alarm businesses; its Residential Builders Commission licenses residential builders and residential specialty trades. Electrical permits and inspections are administered locally.

electricalPermits.notes: City/county building departments issue electrical permits and perform or arrange inspections. The State Fire Marshal's code FAQ says it does not issue building permits; state fire-code oversight is not a statewide electrical-permit program.

agencies.name: South Carolina Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation — Contractor's Licensing Board
agencies.notes: Licenses regulated commercial general and mechanical contracting above $10,000; mechanical classifications include electrical, plumbing and HVAC. Also regulates burglar/fire-alarm businesses under separate alarm licensing provisions. Contractor/qualifying-party licenses are not a universal statewide journeyman-electrician license. Local individual-trade requirements may apply.Ordinary non-alarm low-voltage scope should be checked separately rather than assumed to require an alarm license.

agencies.name: South Carolina Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation — Residential Builders Commission
agencies.notes: Regulates residential builders, residential specialty electrical/plumbing/HVAC contractors and registered residential specialties. Scope differs from the commercial Contractor's Licensing Board. Official Licensee Lookup destination failed to open; no verified direct search or free bulk dataset reported. Permits are local.

agencies.name: South Carolina Law Enforcement Division — Office of Regulatory Services
agencies.notes: Listed for completeness on the security side: SLED licenses private investigative, contract security, and proprietary security businesses and employees (and issues CWP permits). It does NOT license alarm-system installation — burglar alarm and fire alarm system businesses are licensed by the SCLLR Contractor's Licensing Board under the Alarm Systems Business Act (per the CLB's official licensure page). SLED performs criminal-background checks used by SCLLR boards in licensing.

summary: South Dakota has no statewide general-contractor competency license or general HVAC license; local governments set those requirements, and contractors also need the applicable state excise-tax license. State electrical and plumbing commissions license their trades; electrical inspections are divided between the state and authorized municipal programs.

electricalPermits.program: South Dakota Electrical Commission — state wiring permit / electrical inspection program (SDCL ch. 36-16, ARSD ch. 20:44)
electricalPermits.notes: The SD Electrical Commission sells/issues state wiring permits ($15 per permit, books of 20 for contractors; homeowner permit = $20 fee plus inspection fee) and its districted State Electrical Inspectors perform rough-in and final inspections statewide. Per dlr.sd.gov/electrical/inspections.aspx: 'Rapid City and Sioux Falls have local inspection departments for work done within their city limits' — those two cities run their own electrical permit/inspection programs (Sioux Falls also requires its own local electrical contractor license).2023 NEC in effect for permits received on/after Nov. 12, 2024.

agencies.name: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation — Electrical Commission
agencies.notes: Licenses electrical contractors and individual electricians, including journeyman and Class B categories.Contact the Commission for verification.

agencies.name: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation — Plumbing Commission
agencies.notes: Licenses plumbing contractors and individual plumbers and administers plumbing installation oversight. The official consumer page publishes licensee lists; it is a roster gateway rather than an interactive lookup.

agencies.name: South Dakota Department of Revenue — Contractors' Excise Tax
agencies.notes: contractor_license denotes the construction-services excise-tax license only, not a competency or general-contractor occupational license. General building and HVAC licensing is municipal where required; Sioux Falls' mechanical-contractor program is an example.Does not issue electrical permits.

summary: The Board for Licensing Contractors licenses general and trade contractors; a separate board licenses alarm-system contractors. The State Fire Marshal issues electrical permits and inspects where approved local electrical programs do not.

electricalPermits.program: Tennessee Department of Commerce and Insurance — State Fire Marshal, Electrical Inspection Program
electricalPermits.notes: State electrical permits apply outside exempt local inspection jurisdictions.

agencies.name: Tennessee Department of Commerce and Insurance — Board for Licensing Contractors
agencies.notes: Contractor licensing generally begins at $25,000 and includes electrical and mechanical/plumbing/HVAC classifications. Limited Licensed Electrician and Limited Licensed Plumber credentials address smaller work within their statutory/local scope; local acceptance matters. No universal statewide journeyman-electrician license. Certain counties also require home-improvement licensing for smaller covered contracts. Non-alarm low-voltage contracting classification and alarm-board licensing must be distinguished. Current official lookup is the Commerce cloud search.

agencies.name: Tennessee Department of Commerce and Insurance — Alarm Systems Contractors Board
agencies.notes: Licenses alarm-system contracting companies and qualifying agents and registers applicable alarm employees; scope includes burglar/fire alarm and regulated security-system work. Separate from general electrical/mechanical contractor licensing.

agencies.name: Tennessee Department of Commerce and Insurance — State Fire Marshal's Office, Electrical Inspection Program
agencies.notes: Issues electrical permits and arranges inspections in state-served areas; approved local programs are exempt. Website is the Electrical Permits program homepage. Construction/trade-license lookup is handled by the regulatory boards, not this permit entry.

summary: Texas has no statewide general-contractor license; local governments register contractors and issue ordinary electrical permits. TDLR licenses electricians/electrical contractors and HVAC businesses, TSBPE licenses plumbers, DPS regulates security alarms, and the State Fire Marshal regulates fire alarms.

electricalPermits.notes: Electrical permits and inspections are local; TDLR electrical licensing is statewide but does not constitute a statewide electrical work-permit program. No general state electrical-permit lookup applies.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
agencies.notes: Licenses electrical contractors and individual electricians and regulates air-conditioning/refrigeration contractors and technicians. Nonexempt electrical work must be performed under the required electrical credentials. General construction is not a TDLR contractor-licensing program. TDLR All Licenses is the official open dataset. Ordinary low-voltage systems have scope-specific exemptions; security and fire alarms are regulated separately. No state electrical permits issued by TDLR.

agencies.name: Texas State Board of Plumbing Examiners
agencies.notes: Licenses plumbers and regulates Responsible Master Plumbers, through whom plumbing contracting businesses operate. Official free-licensee-list page provides CSV downloads, including responsible master, master and journeyman lists; it is the download landing page, not a single all-license file. Plumbing permits are generally local.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Public Safety — Private Security Program
agencies.notes: Licenses regulated security businesses and individuals, including burglar-alarm and electronic access-control work. TOPS Search Licensees is the official public search reached from the agency-linked portal; individual record retrieval was not tested. This is not a license for all low-voltage data cabling.Does not issue general electrical permits.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Insurance — State Fire Marshal's Office
agencies.notes: Registers fire-alarm companies and licenses applicable fire-alarm personnel; separate from DPS burglar-alarm regulation.Phone is the parent TDI number printed on the SFMO homepage.

summary: DOPL licenses general/specialty contractors, electricians, plumbers and burglar-alarm businesses/personnel; the State Fire Marshal separately certifies fire-alarm inspection/testing personnel. Cities and counties handle ordinary electrical permits, with DFCM enforcing codes for covered state facilities.

electricalPermits.notes: Utah has no statewide electrical permit program; DOPL licenses electricians but does not issue permits or inspect. Electrical permits and inspections are issued by local city/county building departments. Example verified: Salt Lake City Building Services states 'Additional permits may need to be obtained for Electrical, Plumbing, Mechanical, Fire Alarms, and Fire Suppression' and runs its own Citizen Access Portal / SLCPermits.DOPL does run the Utah State Construction Registry a statewide database of construction-project notices (preliminary notices/lien-related filings), not a permitting system.

agencies.name: Utah Department of Commerce — Division of Professional Licensing
agencies.notes: Current agency name is Division of Professional Licensing. Licenses general/residential and specialty contractors, individual electricians/plumbers, and burglar-alarm companies/agents. HVAC contractor H100 requirements changed April 20, 2026; avoid relying solely on older HVAC classification descriptions. Burglar Alarm Company Licensing Act 58-94 is listed as effective January 1, 2027, so is not yet effective at this October 14, 2026 review. Scope-specific low-voltage contractor requirements apply.

agencies.name: Utah Department of Public Safety — State Fire Marshal's Office
agencies.notes: Separately certifies fire-alarm inspection/testing personnel through Basic, Technician and Master categories. These certifications do not replace DOPL contracting/electrical requirements for installation.

agencies.name: Utah Division of Facilities Construction and Management — Building Official
agencies.notes: Building Official oversees code compliance, inspections and approvals for covered state facilities. Ordinary city/county electrical permits remain local.The project's state ownership/jurisdiction must be verified.

summary: Vermont registers covered residential contractors through the Secretary of State's OPR; it has no broad statewide commercial general-contractor license. Public Safety's Division of Fire Safety administers electrical/plumbing credentials and electrical work notices/inspections within statutory jurisdiction, with municipal inspection agreements.

electricalPermits.program: Vermont Department of Public Safety — Division of Fire Safety, Electrical Safety Program
electricalPermits.notes: State electrical work notices and inspections apply to covered complex structures/public buildings, subject to statutory exemptions and municipal inspection agreements. This is not universal state permitting for every owner-occupied single-family dwelling.

agencies.name: Vermont Secretary of State — Office of Professional Regulation
agencies.notes: Residential-contractor registration under 26 V.S.A. chapter 106 covers residential construction contracts above the statutory $10,000 threshold, subject to exemptions; it is not a universal general-contractor competency license. OPR's official 2024 report confirms the registration program began April 1, 2023.

agencies.name: Vermont Department of Public Safety — Division of Fire Safety, Electricians' Licensing Board and Plumbers' Examining Board
agencies.notes: Administers master/journeyman/specialty electrical and plumbing credentials. Electrical contracting is conducted through the applicable licensed master; no separate general-contractor credential is implied. HVAC regulation includes oil/gas heating-technician certification rather than a universal HVAC license. Fire-alarm inspection/testing certification is separately addressed in 20 V.S.A. chapter 173; electrical specialty scope governs relevant wiring.

summary: DPOR's Board for Contractors licenses construction businesses and individual electrical, plumbing and HVAC tradespeople; DCJS separately regulates electronic-security businesses and personnel. Local building departments issue ordinary electrical permits, while DGS administers state-facility building permits.

electricalPermits.notes: Virginia has no state-issued electrical permit program and no state permit lookup. All electrical permits and inspections are issued by local building officials under the Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code (USBC), administered by the VA Dept. of Housing and Community Development (DHCD).com/160/Building-Inspection). Permit lookups exist only at individual locality portals (e.g., county/city citizen-access sites).

agencies.name: Virginia Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation — Board for Contractors
agencies.notes: Licenses contractor businesses by class and specialty and individual tradesmen, including electricians, plumbers and HVAC workers. Electronic/communications work has applicable contractor specialty requirements; DCJS regulates electronic security separately.DPOR does not issue ordinary electrical work permits.

agencies.name: Virginia Department of Criminal Justice Services — Division of Licensure and Regulatory Services
agencies.notes: Licenses private-security businesses and registers applicable electronic-security personnel. Electronic-security business/individual credentials are separate from DPOR construction credentials; fire-alarm-only electrical work should not automatically be classified as private security.

agencies.name: Virginia Department of General Services — Division of Engineering and Buildings
agencies.notes: State Building Official issues permits/approvals for covered state facilities. Website is the division homepage. No trade-license lookup applies.

summary: L&I registers construction contractors, licenses electrical and plumbing businesses/tradespeople, and issues electrical permits and inspections outside approved local electrical jurisdictions. Its Verify tool and state open-data portal provide public contractor records.

electricalPermits.program: Washington Department of Labor & Industries — Electrical Program
electricalPermits.notes: L&I handles electrical permits and inspections except jurisdictions operating their own electrical programs, including the applicable city/Tacoma Power areas. Public search covers L&I electrical and manufactured/mobile-home permits purchased since January 1, 2020, with date-range limits; it does not cover all local permits.

agencies.name: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries
agencies.notes: Registers general/specialty contractors and licenses electrical contractors/electricians and plumbing contractors/plumbers. HVAC construction uses applicable contractor registration plus required electrical/plumbing credentials, not a universal HVAC-technician license. Limited-energy specialty (06) covers fire signaling, intrusion alarms and other specified low-voltage systems; telecommunications contracting has its own scope. HVAC/refrigeration electrical specialty (06A) is distinct from general HVAC business registration. Verify is the public contractor/tradesperson/business tool. Open dataset is L&I Contractor License Data — General, not a complete electrical-permit or every-trade dataset.

agencies.name: Washington State Department of Licensing
agencies.notes: Licenses private security guards, armed private security guards, and private security companies under RCW 18.170 (chapter recodified as 'Security guards'; rules in WAC 308-18) - this is WA's licensing for alarm response/runner and security personnel. Program contact: security@dol.wa.gov. Alarm system INSTALLATION itself is not licensed by DOL; it is L&I electrical licensing (06 limited energy). WA formerly certified 'alarm system agents' under RCW 18.170 but that program was repealed - no separate alarm board exists.

summary: The independent Contractor Licensing Board licenses construction businesses; the Division of Labor certifies plumbers and HVAC technicians, and the State Fire Marshal licenses electricians. Ordinary construction electrical permits are local, with inspections conducted through local requirements and authorized electrical inspectors.

electricalPermits.notes: Municipal/county permitting varies; electrical inspections may be performed by authorized private inspectors, as the City of Ranson's permitting guide demonstrates. State Fire Marshal licensing and fire-safety oversight should not be mistaken for universal state electrical permits.

agencies.name: West Virginia Contractor Licensing Board
agencies.notes: Independent board since June 15, 2021; it is no longer the Division of Labor's contractor-licensing section, though statutory shared services remain. Licenses general/specialty construction businesses, including applicable electrical, plumbing and HVAC classifications. Covered residential projects at $5,000 or more and commercial projects at $25,000 or more trigger contractor licensing, subject to exemptions. Individual trade credentials remain separate.

agencies.name: West Virginia Division of Labor
agencies.notes: Certifies individual plumbers and HVAC technicians; an employer's contractor license does not replace an individual's required certification. Database Searches is the official gateway to plumbing/HVAC verification resources. Its contractor link points to the separate Contractor Licensing Board.

agencies.name: West Virginia Office of the State Fire Marshal
agencies.notes: Licenses master/journeyman/specialty electricians and regulates applicable fire-protection workers. State law provides a specialty electrical credential for low-voltage work at 80 volts or less under defined conditions. Fire-alarm personnel requirements are separate from general contractor licensing.

summary: DSPS credentials dwelling contractors, electricians/electrical contractors, plumbers and HVAC contractors; there is no universal statewide commercial general-contractor license. Municipalities issue many electrical permits, while DSPS handles commercial electrical permits where there is no delegated municipal program and on covered state property.

electricalPermits.program: Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services — Electrical Program
electricalPermits.notes: DSPS issues electrical permits for commercial work in municipalities without delegated electrical inspection authority and for covered state-property work. One- and two-family dwelling enforcement is generally municipal under the UDC. eSLA Public Look-up supports permit/plan-review identifiers and program searches; it is not a guarantee that every local electrical permit is included.

agencies.name: Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services
agencies.notes: Dwelling Contractor and Dwelling Contractor Qualifier credentials apply to covered residential permitting; no general statewide commercial builder license. DSPS licenses electrical contractors and individual electricians, plumbers, and HVAC contractors/qualifiers.Trade applications moved to LicensE January 8, 2024; the DSPS website was redesigned in September 2026. LicensE is the current credential lookup, while eSLA retains permit/plan-review search.DSPS also reviews covered fire-alarm plans but expressly does not issue fire-alarm permits.

summary: Wyoming has no statewide general-contractor, plumbing or HVAC occupational license; cities and counties impose local requirements. The Department of Fire Prevention and Electrical Safety licenses electrical contractors/electricians and handles wiring permits and inspections outside authorized local programs.

electricalPermits.program: Wyoming Department of Fire Prevention and Electrical Safety — Electrical Safety Division
electricalPermits.notes: The state issues wiring permits and conducts inspections in state-served jurisdictions; authorized local electrical jurisdictions handle their own permits/inspections. The official jurisdiction/inspector page should be consulted for the project location.

agencies.name: Wyoming Department of Fire Prevention and Electrical Safety — Electrical Safety Division
agencies.notes: Licenses electrical contractors, master/journeyman electricians and apprentices, with limited/low-voltage categories including LV-A alarm-system work under 90 volts and LV-G covering the listed low-voltage categories. General contractor, plumbing and HVAC licensing remains local where required.Phone is the Cheyenne electrical office number printed on the wiring-permit page.
